# dsh-memory-index
Full-text memory index for DeepSeek Harness.
It indexes the Markdown memory tree you already have — a core `MEMORY.md`, daily notes, a wiki, and
archived sessions — into one local SQLite FTS5 database. It adds `memory_search`, `memory_read`, and
`memory_write`, plus optional startup recall. No embeddings, no API key, no sidecar process, and no
plus optional startup recall. No embeddings, no API key, no sidecar process, and no file migration.
> This is the lexical-first release. Semantic retrieval is planned as an additional layer, not a rep
lacement for the file tree.
## Why this one
Most memory plugins ask you to adopt their storage format. This one assumes your memory is already a
set of Markdown files and makes that tree searchable:
- **Existing files stay authoritative.** `MEMORY.md`, `memory/YYYY-MM-DD.md`, `wiki/`, and `archive/

sessions/` remain ordinary files you can read, edit, `git diff`, or delete.
- **Chinese-friendly ret
rieval.** FTS5 `trigram` when the SQLite build supports it, with a `unicode61` fallback and CJK 3-gr

am expansion.
- **History is searchable.** Archived session Markdown can be indexed next to daily no

tes and long-term memory.
- **Safe defaults.** Read-only, no startup recall, no startup indexing unt

il you ask for it.
- **Local only.** One SQLite file; no network calls and no telemetry.
It is not a replacement for an atomic-fact store, a vector memory service, or an approval-gated `AGE
NTS.md` editor. It solves a narrower problem: *make the memory tree I already write to searchable fr
editor. It solves a narrower problem: *make the memory tree I already write to searchable from DSH.*

## Tools
| Tool | Purpose |
| `memory_search` | Search the configured roots; returns `path:line` and a snippet. Optional `scope`

limits to one source. |
| `memory_read` | Read a file inside a configured memory root. |
| `memory_
write` | Append to today's note, append to the core file, or create/replace a file under a write roo

Commands: `/memory-status`, `/memory-rebuild` (add `fts` to rebuild the full-text table from scratch

## Configuration
[代码示例省略，未执行]
| Field | Default | Meaning |
| `workspace` | required | Directory containing the memory tree. Resolved once and used as the bound

ary for all reads/writes. |
| `indexDb` | `.memory/index.sqlite` | SQLite file, relative to `workspa

ce`, or `:memory:`. |
| `roots` | `MEMORY.md`, `memory/`, `wiki/`, `archive/sessions/` | Files or di
rectories to index. A file root is indexed directly; a directory root is walked recursively. `source

` labels the results. |
| `writeRoots` | `MEMORY.md`, `memory/` | Paths the agent may write. Entries

ending in `.md` are files; others are directories. |
| `digest` | `MEMORY.md`, today, yesterday | O

ptional startup excerpt. `{today}` and `{yesterday}` use `timeZone`. |
| `timeZone` | system zone |

Used for daily-note filenames and digest placeholders. |
| `sourcePriority` | `core`, `daily`, `wiki

`, `session` | Lower ranks first in ties. Unknown sources sort last. |
| `writeMode` | `readonly` |

Set `readwrite` to enable `memory_write`. |
| `autoRecall` | `off` | Set `startup` to add the digest

as prompt context for workspace agents. |
| `buildOnStart` | `false` | Build the index in the backg

round after plugin load. |
| `maxResults` | `8` | Default and cap for `memory_search` (`1`–`20`). |

| `maxFileBytes` | 20 MiB | Files larger than this are skipped. |
| `maxWriteBytes` | 200 KiB | Maxi

mum content accepted by one `memory_write`. |
| `maxDigestChars` | 8000 | Character budget for the s

pted by one `memory_write`. |
| `maxDigestChars` | 8000 | Character budget for the startup digest. |
`roots` and `writeRoots` are independent on purpose: you can index `wiki/` and `archive/sessions/` w
hile allowing writes only to `memory/`.
## Security model

- Every path is resolved inside `workspace`; `..` and absolute escapes are rejected.
- Existing syml
ink components are rejected for reads and writes, so a link inside `memory/` cannot redirect a read

or a write outside the workspace.
- Reads use `O_NOFOLLOW`; writes create a temporary file with mode

`0600`, `fsync`, and rename.
- The core file (`MEMORY.md` by default) is append-only.
- `.env*` fil

es and paths containing `credentials` are excluded from indexing.
- The plugin makes no network requ

d paths containing `credentials` are excluded from indexing.
- The plugin makes no network requests.
## Limitations
- **Lexical, not semantic.** It finds words, not meanings. Embedding-based retrieval is planned as a

n optional layer.
- **No file watcher.** External edits are picked up on the next `/memory-rebuild`

or process start with `buildOnStart`. `memory_write` indexes its own write immediately.
- **Single w
riter.** One process is assumed; SQLite uses a busy timeout, but concurrent writers from multiple pr

ocesses are not coordinated beyond that.
- **No cross-profile sharing by default.** The database liv

es under `workspace/.memory/`; choose a shared `indexDb` only if you understand the locking model.
-
**`node:sqlite` may print an ExperimentalWarning** on Node 22/24. The package targets `^22.19.0 ||

>=24.0.0`.
- **Linux is tested.** Windows and macOS paths are implemented but not yet in CI.
- **App
roximate citations.** A chunk's `line` is its heading/start line; use `memory_read` when exact conte
tations.** A chunk's `line` is its heading/start line; use `memory_read` when exact context matters.
